title: Familiar Shapes: Circles, Triangles, Squares and Rectangles
seo_title: Foundation Shapes Worksheets: Circle, Triangle, Square, Rectangle (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Sort, name and create familiar shapes; recognise and describe familiar shapes within objects in the environment, giving reasons.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on familiar shapes, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFSP01): name circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, count sides and corners, sort and find shapes around us. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Count the sides and corners to name a shape.
key_sub: Turning, colour and size never change a shape's name.
body_html:
Four shapes

A circle is round. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. A square has 4 sides that are all the same. A rectangle has 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short.

Turning, colour and size

A shape keeps its name when it is turned, coloured or made bigger. A square on its corner is still a square.

Shapes around us

Look for shapes in everyday things: a plate is a circle, a door is a rectangle. Say why: count the sides and corners.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Calling a turned square a diamondCount the sides: 4 equal sides is a square
Calling a long rectangle a squareA square has all 4 sides the same
Saying a circle has cornersA circle is round: no corners

faq.q: What shapes do Foundation students learn?
faq.a: Familiar shapes like circles, triangles, squares and rectangles. They sort, name and make them, and find them in everyday objects, giving reasons (AC9MFSP01).

faq.q: Is a square on its corner a diamond?
faq.a: It is still a square. Turning a shape does not change its name. Count the sides: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners.
Yes, a square is a special rectangle with all four sides the same length. At Foundation we mostly call it a square.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn shapes?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt at home or in the park: a clock is a circle, a door is a rectangle. Ask: How do you know? How many sides?
